what_happened: The job was asked to cut the time of the slow athena-cli test binaries (lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry, steward) so a full `cargo test` runs under 7 minutes. The verifier rejected it with 2 of 6 acceptance criteria unmet and 3 blocker or major findings. The unmet criteria: (a) docs/decisions.md needs a decision with measured before and after times per binary, with the cause found for each and the total suite time; (b) `cargo test --locked` must pass with every test running in under 7 minutes. The findings say the goal was not met, and the change admits this in its own Goal check. The planned per-binary test changes were never made. The cause was found for lifecycle only, and the other four binaries were inferred. No failed check is named. The job wrote up its result (decision D126) but did not do the work.
cause: The 7-minute target was set without a measured per-binary baseline or a budget saying how much each binary must give up. Nothing checked during the work whether the planned changes could reach the target. The producer was allowed to finish by documenting a miss and partial findings instead of failing early or reporting the shortfall. A write-up criterion (D126 with measured times and causes) could be met in form while the real goal was not, and only the final verifier compared the outcome to the target. This is the same gap as the earlier speedup job: no baseline, no early reachability check.
prevention: Add a measure-first stage to speed-target jobs. Before the producer edits anything, it records a baseline wall time for each binary and the total, using one fixed method. The plan must then give each binary a time budget that adds up to the target, with the cause found by measurement for each. The producer must run the suite after each binary's change and stop with a clear shortfall report if the running total cannot reach the target. A decision write-up that admits the goal was missed must not count as done. It should fail the job early as a partial result, with the measured causes kept.
proposed_request: Cut the full `cargo test --locked` wall time to under 7 minutes without weakening any test. Work in two steps. Step 1: on the job's machine, measure and record a baseline for each athena-cli test binary (lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry, steward) and for the whole suite, using the same method for every figure. Find each binary's cause of slowness by measurement, not inference. Step 2: change only test code and test helpers (crates/athena-cli/tests/*.rs and common/mod.rs). Do not change production code or production defaults. After each binary's change, re-measure it the same way. Acceptance: (1) a new decision in docs/decisions.md lists per-binary before and after times labeled measured, the measured cause for each of the five binaries, and the total suite time; (2) `cargo test --locked` passes with every test still running, and the total is under 7 minutes on the job's machine; (3) a deliberately failing test still fails the run; (4) no file outside the test files and docs/decisions.md changed. If the running total shows the target is unreachable by test-only changes, stop and report the measured shortfall per binary instead of finishing with a document that admits the miss.
